transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

My mind just doesn’t seem to work the way it used to—I can’t think straight or make simple decisions anymore. It feels like a constant fog, and I just get completely stuck trying to do everyday tasks.
Along with this mental fog, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Yes, most days I wake up with a heavy, sinking feeling in my chest that stays with me all day, making me feel like there's no point to anything. I've also completely stopped going to my watercolor classes and genealogy trips because the thought of being around people or trying to enjoy myself just feels like too much effort.
Have you recently experienced any physical illnesses, medical conditions, or head injuries around the time these symptoms started?

No, I haven't had any head injuries or major new illnesses myself, just my usual aging aches and pains. It was actually my older sister who developed serious heart problems about a year and a half ago, and taking on her care has been incredibly stressful.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, depressed mood and the difficulty concentrating?

It’s been going on for a long time now, probably a little over a year. It really started sinking in shortly after I took over my sister's care, so it's getting close to a year and a half that I've been feeling this heavy and foggy.
Along with the mental fog, do you experience persistent physical exhaustion or bodily weakness even after doing very light physical tasks?
I wouldn't say I feel physically exhausted or weak in that way. It's more that I feel extremely slowed down and sluggish, almost like my body is moving underwater whenever I try to do simple things.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since you started feeling this way?

Yes, I've really lost my appetite over the past year—food doesn't appeal to me anymore, so I often just pick at my meals or forget to eat, and my clothes have gotten noticeably looser. As for my sleep, I haven't really noticed any major changes in my patterns.
During this difficult time, have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness, or have you been blaming yourself excessively for things?

Yes, I feel incredibly useless and overwhelmed, especially when I struggle to manage my sister's care. I constantly feel like I must have done something terribly wrong, which is why I'm convinced the hospital staff is quietly working against us and changing her charts.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of severe depression or a time when you felt this down in the past, or is this the very first time in your life you've felt this way?
No, I don't recall ever feeling this bad or having a period like this in the past. This is really the first time in my life I've felt so completely overwhelmed and down. It all feels very new to me.
Have you recently heard any voices or seen things that other people cannot see or hear?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't hear any strange voices or see things that aren't really there.
You mentioned believing the hospital staff is changing your sister's charts. Do you feel like other people are also watching you, plotting against you, or trying to harm you?

No, I don't feel like random people are watching me or trying to harm me in general. It's really just some of the doctors and nurses at my sister's hospital who I'm convinced are quietly working against us, changing her charts or delaying things because of something I must have done wrong.
